newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils close lower despite Chicago gain.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils close lower despite Chicago gain.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices closed lower on Tuesday despite gains in Chicago soy oil futures as players dumped soy meal for oil.
Key market data released in Malaysian during Tuesday morning was the main factor in the palm oil market while a slightly easier dollar was behind the lower drift in soft oils.

The Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) said early on Tuesday that palm oil stocks at the end of March stood at 689,633 tonnes against 723,399 at end-February, while exports were running at 565,219 tonnes during March against 380,267 during the holiday-affected month of February.
PORLA said output rose 35.7 percent in March to 683,196 tonnes.
Traders said based on the stock figure the report had looked bullish at first but when the output figure was taken into consideration they changed their views.
"If output is running at this level now, we can see it at 800,000 tonnes a month during the peak production months of July through to October," said one.
Traders said Malaysian exports were not at a high enough level to take-up the increased production because prices were too high.
"Some countries who normally buy palm oil are buying soft oils because they are cheaper.
European traders also expressed doubts over the local disappearance rate which was around 151,000 tonnes in March when it is normally under 100,000 tonnes.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $5 to $7.50 a tonne down while products were $2.50 to $5 lower with further business reported during the afternoon.

Coconut oil sellers closed lower under pressure from origin at $5 to $7.50 down after Mar/Apr traded at $717.50, Apr/May at $712.50 and $710, May/Jun at $707.50 and $700 and Jun/Jul $705 and $700 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil finished $2.50 down and tradeless.

In soft oils Dutch soy oil closed 0.75 guilders down after Aug/Sep traded at 104 guilders and rape oil finished unchanged to 0.50 guilders lower after May/Jul fetched 104.25 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
